subject: Proposed Platform/Serving Span Merge — draft comms + QBR talking points
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed Platform/Serving Span Merge — initial draft + QBR posture

Team,

Quick note to share a working draft of a proposed organizational change: merge Platform (infra/runtime) and Serving (model-serving, runtime ops) into a single "Platform & Serving" span under an SVP-level leader. The goal is tighter ownership of end-to-end inference economics and a cleaner handoff for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Why now (short):
- Repeated friction points across release and rollout between runtime kernel changes and serving orchestration (latency slippage in canaries)
- Customers like Acme are asking for a single owner for inference SLAs + performance guarantees
- Q3 OKRs push toward a unified cost/perf story — this alignment reduces cross-squad dependencies

What I'm asking: please review the attached one-pager (span_merge_plan_v1.pdf) and the QBR bullets (first pass) and give strategic feedback by EOD Wednesday. Specifically:
1) Any major operational risk I missed?
2) Suggested changes to the comms tone (soft vs. firm on role moves)
3) Names to consult before we share with execs (external partners if needed)

I've included proposed talking points that we can use in the QBR readout and a timeline that preserves ongoing critical hires. This is still a draft — I want to ensure we have a clean message for both internal teams and our top customers.

Next steps: I'll incorporate feedback and circulate an exec-facing one-slide and a staff FAQ.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Platform Strategy | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Proposed Platform/Serving Span Merge — initial draft + QBR posture

Marissa — thanks for pulling this together. Quick notes after a read: 

- High level: I agree with the rationale. The customer-facing narrative is sensible (single owner for latency/cost).
- Operational risk: we need clearer transition steps for the runtime reliability pager and the Dedicated capacity SLOs. Suggest adding an explicit 30/60/90 day ops checklist in the one-pager (who owns what on day 1 vs. month 2).
- Tone: for staff comms, call out that most individual contributors' roles remain the same; emphasize that this is about removing handoffs, not headcount changes. Avoid words like "merge" in the all-hands subject line — use "unified span" or "streamlined platform model."

I'll flag RINF-914 in my notes — we can tie the Jira to the FAQ for technical details. Also recommend a short sync with CS (include Connor O'Brien) before we send anything to top customers — we should ensure support/incident routing is mapped.

One nit: in the QBR bullets, the second metric still references old 'kernel-latency' nomenclature. Suggest we show 'end-to-end inference P95' instead (customers care about end-to-end).

Happy to review a 2nd pass.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber | VP Product Strategy

Staff FAQ (excerpt):
Q: Will my role change?
A: Most individual contributor roles will not change. Managers will see scope realignment; we'll share role-specific notes in manager packets.

Q: Why now?
A: Consolidation reduces handoffs and clarifies ownership for inference SLAs and customer-facing performance commitments.

Q: Hiring impact?
A: We are requesting approval to repurpose two open IC requisitions to Serving runtime; no layoffs planned.
